content.text: Both bugs are clear from the code. `%W`/`%w` use Sunday-based weeks, not ISO weeks, so I'll switch to `date.fromisocalendar`. The holiday argument is never read, so I'll make the loop check it.

"""Business-day arithmetic."""

from datetime import date, timedelta


def business_days(start, end, holidays=()):
    """Count weekdays in [start, end), skipping any date in `holidays`."""
    holiday_set = set(holidays)
    days = 0
    d = start
    while d < end:
        if d.weekday() < 5 and d not in holiday_set:
            days += 1
        d += timedelta(days=1)
    return days
EOF
cat > cal/isoweek.py <<'EOF'
"""ISO week dates like 2026-W05-3."""

import re
from datetime import date

_ISO_WEEK_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{4})-W(\d{2})-([1-7])$")


def parse_iso_week(text):
    """Return the date for an ISO week date string YYYY-Www-D (Monday=1 .. Sunday=7)."""
    m = _ISO_WEEK_RE.match(text)
    if not m:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid ISO week date: {text!r}")
    year, week, weekday = (int(g) for g in m.groups())
    return date.fromisocalendar(year, week, weekday)
EOF

python -c "from cal.isoweek import parse_iso_week as p; print(p('2026-W05-3'))"

"""ISO week dates like 2026-W05-3."""

import re
from datetime import date

_ISO_WEEK_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{4})-W(\d{2})-([1-7])$")


def parse_iso_week(text):
    """Return the date for an ISO week date string YYYY-Www-D (Monday=1 .. Sunday=7)."""
    m = _ISO_WEEK_RE.match(text)
    if not m:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid ISO week date: {text!r}")
    year, week, weekday = (int(g) for g in m.groups())
    return date.fromisocalendar(year, week, weekday)
